title: Method transfer: 'Process fairness estimation via feature selection' (W2617709446, cluster 8) may address an open limitation in W2964316623 (cluster 9)
explanation: Paper openalex:W2617709446 (cluster 8) has a method-type claim semantically close (cosine 0.759) to the work of openalex:W2964316623 (cluster 9), which reports an own-work limitation — yet the two clusters are weakly citation-bridged (1 edges) and openalex:W2617709446's method(s) are absent from cluster 9. Method(s): Process fairness estimation via feature selection. B's limitation: "Survey responses rely on self-reported ratings which may introduce self-report biases.". SEMANTIC SHORTLIST (claim-embedding cosine), NOT an LLM-confirmed 'addresses' verdict — a lead to check, not a finding.

caveats.label: Mixed-fidelity
caveats.detail: 1 supporting paper(s) are abstract-only, which yield ~11x fewer own-work limitations than full text.

caveats.label: Semantic lead
caveats.detail: A semantic shortlist LLM-confirmed as 'not_addressing' — a lead, not a finding.

consumer.headline: “Process fairness estimation via feature selection” might solve a problem reported by “Human Perceptions of Fairness in Algorithmic Decision Making”
consumer.kind_short: A method from one area that might solve a problem in another
consumer.kind_long: Two groups of papers that barely cite each other. One group has a method; the other reports a problem that method looks related to. Nobody appears to have tried connecting them — but we matched them by similarity, so this needs a human to check whether the connection is real.
consumer.strength_meaning: This is a pattern we spotted automatically and have not verified. Treat it as a hint to investigate, not a finding.
consumer.why: One paper has a method. Another reports a problem the method looks related to. We matched them by comparing how the two papers are worded — which is a starting point, not proof.

caveats.label: Based partly on summaries only
caveats.text: For some of these papers we only had the summary, not the full text. Papers we could read in full reveal far more about their own limits, so this may be built on an incomplete picture.

caveats.label: A promising match we haven't verified
caveats.text: We matched these two papers because their wording is close, not because anyone confirmed the connection makes sense. It may not survive contact with an expert.

caveats.label: Checked — the method doesn't address the problem
caveats.text: On re-reading, the method does not actually address the problem it was matched to.

consumer.verdict_reason: A language-model check found that the method does not actually address this problem; the two are related in topic only.
